🚀 RAG Tutor — Notebook 3: Common Improvements for Production

Visualizing Hybrid Search (RRF), Cross-Encoder Slopegraphs & Agentic RAG

A basic 50-line vector RAG works great for simple demos, but in production systems it runs into three classic failure modes:
  1. Exact Keyword Blindness: Dense vectors compress a whole passage into one vector and often miss exact error codes, part numbers, or function names (solved by Hybrid Search).
  2. Noisy Bi-Encoder Distractors: Chunks that mention the same general topic without answering the specific question sneak into the Top ||(K||) (solved by Cross-Encoder Reranking).
  3. Multi-Hop & Unverified Answers: Single-shot retrieval fails when a user asks a multi-part question spanning multiple documents (solved by Agentic RAG).

1. Hybrid Search: BM25 Keyword + Vector Similarity + Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines the rank positions from Okapi BM25 (exact keyword match) and Cosine Similarity (semantic meaning) without needing to normalize incompatible raw score scales: ||[\text{RRF\_Score}(d) = \frac{\alpha}{k + \text{rank}_{\text{vector}}(d)} + \frac{1 - \alpha}{k + \text{rank}_{\text{bm25}}(d)}||]Drag Fusion Weight ||(\alpha||) and RRF Constant ||(k||) below to watch the Stacked RRF Decomposition Bars (left) and the Rank Discount Curve (right) shift in real time:

2. Cross-Encoder Reranking (STAGE2-RERANK-15to3)

Bi-encoders embed the query and each chunk separately, which is fast for searching thousands of rows in DuckDB, but misses fine-grained token-to-token interactions. A Cross-Encoder Reranker scores each candidate (query, chunk) pair together, promoting direct answers above the Top-||(K||) Cutoff Line and pushing down noisy distractors!

Step 3: Grounded Answer (ggml-org/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF:Q8_0 · 3621 ms)

To answer a multi-hop question like this, an agentic RAG system would first use Query Decomposition & Rewriting to split the request into targeted sub-queries, such as "DuckDB error ERR-VEC-768 cause and fix" and "two-stage cross-encoder reranking pattern STAGE2-RERANK-15to3" [Chunk #31]. Regarding the two-stage reranking pattern, STAGE2-RERANK-15to3 improves precision by using a two-stage process [Chunk #26]: 1. Stage 1 (Fast Recall): It uses Hybrid Search (combining DuckDB Vector and BM25) to quickly retrieve the top 15 to 25 candidate chunks in about 5–15 milliseconds [Chunk #26]. 2. Stage 2 (High-Precision Rerank): Only these 15–25 candidates are then passed through for a high-precision rerank [Chunk #26]. Hybrid Search is beneficial because pure vector search can struggle with exact error codes and diagnostic identifiers, such as ERR-VEC-768 [Chunk #20].
